title: Pattachitra with Kali defeating Shiva
maker: Not individually identified by the gallery
description: Maker: Not individually identified by the gallery. Medium: coloured pigments on paper. The gallery labels this work public domain but sets image reproduction conditions; its image is not reproduced here.

title: Madhubani painting
maker: Bhuvana Meenakshi, as identified by the uploader
imageAlt: Concentric rings of blue, green and yellow motifs within a patterned rectangular border
credit: Bhuvana Meenakshi, Madhubani painting. CC BY-SA 3.0. Reproduction resized.
description: Maker: Bhuvana Meenakshi, as identified by the uploader. Medium: Not specified in available record.

title: Untitled (Tree of Life)
imageAlt: Two women gather flowers beneath a tree filled with black birds
credit: Durgabai Vyam, © Sarmaya Arts Foundation, 2015.2.24. CC BY 4.0. Reproduction resized.
description: Sarmaya identifies this Gond-Pardhan painting as an undated work in gouache and ink, accession 2015.2.24.

title: Warli-style acrylic painting on canvas
description: The uploader describes this as Warli art. The maker of the depicted work and community identity are not established.

title: Kalamkari Panel with Niche
medium: Cotton, plain weave, mordant painted and dyed, resist dyed
imageAlt: A pointed arch edged with scrolling flowers on a tall cotton panel
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Frederic B. Pratt, 1927, 27.215.1. CC0. Reproduction resized.
description: The Met attributes this painted and dyed cotton to Burhanpur in the Deccan. The maker is not identified.

title: Figure of Hindu god Ganesh, Dhokra style
description: The Science Museum Group records this nineteenth-century figure in the Dhokra style. Consult the museum record for its details and image terms.

title: Krishna’s Dance of Delight (Rasa Lila)
description: LACMA credits both named makers. Its online record does not provide an image.

title: Three Dancing Women
description: LACMA identifies Bhagawati Devi as the maker; follow the source for the object and image terms.

title: Brahma and Vishnu
description: The LACMA record identifies the maker, place and date.

title: Gond: Deer with Foxes
description: Sarmaya describes the imagery and identifies Durga Bai as the artist.

title: Gond: Dancing Elephants
description: Sarmaya identifies Durga Bai as the artist.

title: Warli Painting 17
medium: Rice juice and cow dung on paper
description: Fukuoka Asian Art Museum documents this painting. Its reproduction terms do not permit an embedded image here.

title: Holi and Village Tradition
description: Fukuoka Asian Art Museum documents this work. Its reproduction terms do not permit an embedded image here.

title: Panel
medium: Cotton; mordant painted and dyed, resist dyed
description: The Met identifies this textile as kalamkari and marks its image public domain.
imageAlt: A cotton panel seen obliquely, with repeated red flowering sprigs across the field
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Yukikazu Iwasa, in memory of Seizaburo and Shizuko Iwasa, 2009, 2009.172. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Kalamkari Rumal
medium: Cotton; mordant painted and dyed, resist dyed
description: The Met marks this image public domain.
imageAlt: A red-bordered painted cloth filled with small figures and narrative scenes
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1928, 28.159.3. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Figurine of the Hindu god Vishnu, Dhokra style
description: The Science Museum Group describes the identification of the figure as Vishnu as uncertain.

title: Moonshadow Longpi Stambh
description: An account of the Stambh exhibition quotes the atelier describing this work as three stacked vases. The project credits Ashiesh Shah as artist and designer; the individual potters are not identified.

title: The avatar Narasimha
medium: Watercolor, colloidal tin, ink and graphite on mill paper
description: The Met marks this image public domain.
imageAlt: Narasimha, with a lion’s head and human body, holds a figure across his lap
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Bequest of Robert West, by exchange, 2022, 2021.425. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Ajrakh block-printed scarf with embroidery
maker: Sufiyan Ismail Khatri and Asif Shaikh
description: The museum credits Sufiyan Ismail Khatri with block printing and Asif Shaikh with the embroidery.

title: Kantha (Embroidered Quilt)
description: The Philadelphia Museum of Art discusses scenes of daily life in this quilt.

title: Kantha (Embroidered Quilt)
description: The Philadelphia Museum of Art describes the image of Durga in this quilt.

title: Lidded Bidri ware vase
description: The Horniman Museum describes the inlaid lidded vase and its detached chain.

title: Bidri Flower Vase or Phooldan
description: Salar Jung Museum describes a flower vase with inlaid decoration.

title: Phad Painting
description: The Crafts Museum credits Prakash Joshi with this painting on its entrance gate.

title: Inta wall plaque
description: The Syracuse University Art Museum records this plaque as coming from Molela, Rajasthan.

title: Molela plaque depicting Ganesha
description: The South Asia Collection describes the plaque and places its origin in Molela.

title: Wooden figure representing a sister
description: The Research Center for Material Culture identifies this Channapatna figure as part of a brother-and-sister pair, object TM-3247-18a.

title: Embroidered textile border
description: Penn Museum attributes the border to Kutch and describes the chain-stitch embroidery.

title: Wall hanging
medium: Cotton fabric with embroidery, satin stitches
description: The Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art describes this object as a hanging or cover for wedding food gifts.

title: Hanuman carrying Rama and Lakshmana on his two shoulders
description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art attributes this painting to an unidentified artist working in Kolkata.

title: Kantha
description: The Cleveland Museum of Art identifies this embroidered and quilted cotton as a nineteenth-century work from Bengal.
imageAlt: Cream cotton quilt stitched with figures, animals and floral designs
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of William E. Ward in memory of his wife, Evelyn Svec Ward, 1996.350. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Bidri Basin
medium: Zinc alloy with silver and brass inlay
description: The Cleveland Museum of Art identifies this wide-rimmed basin as made in Bidar, Karnataka.
imageAlt: A low dark basin with silver and brass floral inlay along its broad rim
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund, 2020.205. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Cover (Rumal)
description: The Met records this embroidered cover as a work from Chamba. Its description identifies Radha and Krishna in a grove.
imageAlt: Black-and-white museum photograph of an embroidered cover with figures and trees in a grove
credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Friedsam Collection, Bequest of Michael Friedsam, 1931, 32.100.462. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Hanging (Phulkari work)
description: The Cleveland Museum of Art records this embroidered hanging as a work from Punjab.
imageAlt: An embroidered hanging with a dense repetition of geometric motifs
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. J. Livingstone Taylor, 1942.367. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Head and body mask of Kaliya
description: An academic museum publication identifies this mask as made by the workshop at Samaguri and records it in the British Museum, inventory 2015,3041.1.

title: Aranmula Mirror
description: Sanskriti Museums describes a circular metal mirror set in an ornate frame.

title: Tsüngkotepsü — Naga Shawl
date: Not stated in the online record
description: The National Crafts Museum records this shawl under accession 85/6861 and locates it in Nagaland.

title: Natraja
medium: Natural colour on cloth and wood
description: The National Museum lists this Tanjore-style painting as accession 75.355.

title: Hand painted Plates
description: Dastkari Haat Samiti credits the makers and identifies Qamar Dagar as a guide for the project.

title: The Rock Garden of Chandigarh
date: Begun 1957, according to the district account
medium: Reused ceramics, stone and other recovered materials
description: A sculptural environment, rather than a single portable object. Chandigarh district names Nek Chand as its founder; many people contributed to its history.

title: Wall Plaque
date: Not stated in the online record
description: The National Crafts Museum describes a round papier-mâché wall plaque, accession 84/217, from Jammu and Kashmir.

title: Aipan mural, Khati
maker: Poornima Sukumar and Wise Wall Project collaborators
description: Project FUEL says its head artist Poornima Sukumar conceptualised the murals with community contributions and shows her painting an Aipan pattern.

title: Kaavi art at the Convent of Santa Monica
description: A photograph documents a Kaavi surface revealed during restoration at the convent in Old Goa. The record does not identify the artist or date the wall art.
holding: Convent of Santa Monica, Old Goa
imageAlt: Red floral and animal motifs follow the curve of a pale plaster arch above an iron gate
credit: Photograph by Aren Noronha. CC BY-SA 4.0. Reproduction resized.

title: Sohrai paintings at Sanskriti Museum
maker: Santhal women artists; individuals not identified in source
medium: Paint on surfaces; see the source
description: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs describes a photographed group of works at the Sanskriti Museum and Art Gallery, Hazaribagh.

title: Zari Zardozi: Making of zari embroidery
description: Dastkari Haat Samiti documents a work in progress in its account of Delhi zardozi.

title: Cheriyal mural for the Pari project
date: Date not stated in the source
description: Lalit Kala Akademi credits Sai Kiran and illustrates a mural in its Pari project artist note.

title: Villianur terracotta design collection
maker: NIFT Chennai students, V. K. Munusamy and Karunanithi
description: NIFT describes a collaborative collection of outdoor décor, lighting and other objects developed with master artisans and students. This record refers to the collection, not one object.

title: Coconut-shell turtles at Kavaratti
description: The Max Planck Institute for the History of Science captions a photograph of a display of coconut-shell turtles at the Handicrafts Museum, Kavaratti. The record refers to a group, not a single object.

title: Mithun-shaped Mon Shugu paper
description: A Mithun-shaped handmade paper component of the 2026 Republic Day invitation kit. The National Institute of Design describes the collaboration with artisans; it does not identify the individual maker of this component.

title: Lepcha woven and embroidered panel
description: A woven and embroidered component of the 2026 Republic Day invitation kit, described by the National Institute of Design as reflecting a connection to the mountains. The individual maker is not identified.

title: Puan Chei textile component
description: A Puan Chei textile component of the collaborative 2026 Republic Day invitation kit. The National Institute of Design describes the weaving; it does not name the individual artisan responsible for this component.

title: Eri silk chaddar
description: A woman’s wrapper made in Meghalaya, measuring 65 × 187 cm. The Mississippi Entomological Museum describes the preparation of its silk and records the year; the maker is not named.

title: Risha from the Reang community
description: A Risha from the Reang community pictured in a research project by Aratrik Dev Varman and Jisha Unnikrishnan. The page does not identify the weaver or date this individual textile.

title: Pandanus mat in the making
description: A mat being made is pictured as figure 24 in a 2008 ethnobotanical study of the Nicobar Islands. The source does not name the maker; its historical descriptions include language that readers may find outdated.

title: Panja durrie in a field study
description: A 2018 field study discusses Panipat production and takes a panja durrie as an object of study. The abstract does not give an individual maker, date or object image.

title: Genduk Choknis
description: In an interview, thangka artist Tonyot Tashi names Genduk Choknis among paintings displayed in museums. The interview does not assign this painting to a specific institution or date it.

title: Jagannatha, Balabhadra, and Subhadra in the Jagannatha Temple
holding: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
credit: Los Angeles County Museum of Art, Indian Art Special Purpose Fund, M.82.107. Public domain. Reproduction resized.
description: LACMA describes this as a Puri pilgrimage painting. The temple complex and surrounding shrines share the same field, with the deities at its centre.
imageAlt: A painted plan of the Jagannath temple at Puri with colourful shrines and figures

title: Bidri Hookah Bowl with Roses
medium: Zinc alloy with silver and brass inlay
description: Repeated inlaid rose bushes give this vessel a rhythm that changes as it turns. Cleveland dates the bowl to the seventeenth century.
imageAlt: Flowering rose bushes in pale inlay around a dark, rounded hookah bowl
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Severance and Greta Millikin Purchase Fund, 2020.207. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Nataraja, Shiva as the Lord of Dance
description: The figure balances on one leg inside a circle of fire. Cleveland attributes this bronze to the Chola period in Tamil Nadu.
imageAlt: A bronze Shiva dancing with four arms inside a ring of flames
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, 1930.331. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Shrine with a Seated Male Deity
description: Cleveland identifies the shrine as Kerala-style. The figure and its architectural frame are catalogued as parts of one bronze object.
imageAlt: A seated bronze deity framed by the supports and roof of a small shrine
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Dr. Norman Zaworski, 2011.206. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Krishna Vanquishing the Crane-Demon Bakasura
medium: gum tempera and gold on paper
description: Cleveland places the painting in Tirupati. The diagonal connects Krishna’s exertion to the falling crane demon.
imageAlt: Krishna confronts the crane demon in a scene arranged along a strong diagonal
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1966.29. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Part of a Skirt (Ghaghara)
medium: silk satin embroidered with silk in "ari" chain stitch
description: The continuous chain stitch on the reverse helps identify the hooked awl used to create the repeating vines. Cleveland attributes the textile to Gujarat, possibly Kutch.
imageAlt: A long dark silk panel with rows of embroidered flowers and blue tassels at one end
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, 1925.794. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Border Fragment of a Shawl
description: This woven fragment survives from the border of a larger shawl. The Kashmiri pattern was designed to read as a repeat on a moving garment.
imageAlt: A wool shawl border woven with bright teardrop-shaped floral motifs
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the Cleveland School of Art, 1934.199. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Bedspread
description: Cleveland’s record identifies biblical scenes, Indian mythological figures and Portuguese costume on this embroidered textile from Goa.
imageAlt: A bedspread embroidered with rows of figures around a patterned centre
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Norweb Collection, 1969.295. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Pendants
medium: Gilt silver with diamonds, emeralds, rubies, pearls, and enamel
description: The museum identifies the fish as an auspicious motif and gives two possible uses for these ornaments, as earrings or as pendants suspended from a crown.
imageAlt: Matching jeweled pendants, each with a fish at the centre
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. J. H. Wade, 1916.280. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: A princess with attendants on a terrace
medium: Gum tempera and gold on paper
description: Cleveland attributes the painting to eighteenth-century Hyderabad in the Deccan.
imageAlt: A princess and attendants on a terrace in a Deccani court painting
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift in honor of Madeline Neves Clapp; Gift of Mrs. Henry White Cannon by exchange; Bequest of Louise T. Cooper; Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund; From the Catherine and Ralph Benkaim Collection, 2013.291. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Dancing Ganesha
description: The dancing figure is carved in sandstone. Cleveland locates the work in central India, in Madhya Pradesh.
imageAlt: A carved stone Ganesha with bent legs and six arms
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1961.93. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Mother Goddess
description: Cleveland identifies this as part of a group of mother goddesses from the Udaipur district. The gesture toward the child gives the sculpture a point of focus.
imageAlt: A standing stone figure gently holds a child by the wrist
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, 1970.12. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Agni, God of Fire
description: Cleveland identifies the figure as Agni, with flames behind him and a goat below. The figures above him broaden the scene to include fire rites.
imageAlt: A carved male deity with flames behind him and small figures above
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Edward L. Whittemore Fund, 1955.51. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: The Marriage of Rukmini [Mangal]
medium: Gum tempera and gold on paper
description: Cleveland identifies this marriage scene as a work of the Garhwal school in the Pahari Hills.
imageAlt: Figures in a yellow palace, beneath a pavilion and beside a walled garden
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Maxeen and John Flower in honor of Dr. Stanislaw Czuma, 2011.138. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Standing Devi
description: Cleveland attributes this twelfth-century brass figure to Ladakh.
imageAlt: A standing brass goddess with a narrow waist and an elaborate headdress
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Bequest of Mrs. Severance A. Millikin, 1989.370. CC0. Reproduction resized.

title: Illustration of the Mahabharata
description: Cleveland identifies this scene from the Mahabharata as a work of the Paithan school in Maharashtra.
imageAlt: Figures painted in bold outlines and flat colours in a scene from the Mahabharata
credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. William E. Ward, 1988.121. CC0. Reproduction resized.
